title: Controlling a stage: activities, inputs, outputs and RACI
blurb: Place a project manager's action in the right controlling a stage activity, judge it against the recommended actions and name who is accountable, responsible, consulted or informed.
question: During a delivery stage, the project manager fixes a two-week slip on one work package by re-sequencing later work, staying inside stage tolerance. Which activity is this, which activity puts the fix into effect, and which role is accountable?

teach.h: Controlling a stage in a Practitioner question
teach.body: Controlling a stage is the project manager's day-to-day process: assign work, monitor it, handle issues, report progress to the board and take corrective action so the stage stays inside the tolerances the board set. It starts when the board authorizes a stage or an exception plan. Practitioner questions give you a scenario action and ask which of the eight activities it belongs to, whether it follows the recommended actions, or which role holds A, R, C or I.

teach.h: An issue or risk turns up

root.label: Capture issues and risks
root.sub: register it, then assess its impact

children.label: Take corrective action
children.sub: then authorize a new or amended WP

teach.caption: A work-package-level breach that the PM can absorb inside stage tolerance is not escalated to the board; it is handled by corrective action and shown in the next highlight report.

items: Authorize a work package: define it, co-create and review it with the team manager, confirm acceptance, then authorize the start.
Evaluate work package status: hold informal conversations with the team manager, review the checkpoint report, update the stage plan, and update the project log if needed.
Receive completed work package: make sure each product has the approval its product description requires, then update the product register and stage plan.
Take corrective action: collect facts about the deviation, find and select a solution, then trigger it through authorize a work package.
Report highlights: assemble checkpoint reports, the project log and stage plan revisions, list the corrective actions taken, and issue the highlight report.

rows.label: Situation
values: Stage tolerance forecast to be exceeded

rows.label: What happens next
values: Board decides; may ask for an exception plan

teach.caption: Exception means a FORECAST breach. The PM does not wait for the overspend or delay to happen.

teach.h: Controlling a stage: the RACI rows to know
head: Activity
Role
RACI
teach.caption: From the official RACI extracts for table 16.2 (16.6). Look up any other row in the open book.

teach.body: Accountable is the one role that answers for the outcome: for take corrective action that is the executive, even though the project manager does the work. Responsible is the role that does it. Consulted roles give input before it is done; informed roles are told afterwards. 'Not involved' is not the same as informed: the business layer has no part in taking corrective action. Read the question for which letter it wants, then find the row in table 16.2.

teach.h: Worked scenario: Brennan Mutual, Project Skyline (S6)
teach.body: In the wave migration stage, Stratoshift's delivery lead Arjun Menon reports in his checkpoint that test environments arrived late, so his work package will finish nine days behind its time tolerance. Project manager Mairi Campbell captures the issue in the issue register and assesses it: the stage can absorb the slip. In take corrective action she moves two applications into a later wave and amends Arjun's work package with him through authorize a work package. Executive Fraser McIntyre is accountable; project support is informed and updates the registers. No exception report is needed.

teach.text: Classic traps: (1) Corrective action is put into effect THROUGH authorize a work package. (2) Capture means register first, then assess, before choosing a response. (3) An exception report is raised only when STAGE (or project) tolerance is forecast to be exceeded; a work package breach the PM can absorb stays in controlling a stage. (4) The exception plan is prepared later, in managing a stage boundary, not in controlling a stage.

items: Work package activities: authorize, evaluate status, receive completed.
Monitoring and reporting: evaluate stage status, report highlights.
Problems: capture issues and risks, take corrective action, escalate issues and risks.
Report highlights: PM responsible; team manager, project support and project assurance consulted.
Take corrective action: executive accountable, PM responsible, project support informed.

summary: You can now place any project manager action in the right controlling a stage activity, from co-creating a work package to escalating a forecast breach. You can also answer RACI questions on report highlights and take corrective action from the official rows.

A.q: Brennan Mutual's Project Skyline is in its wave migration stage. Project manager Mairi Campbell has a short call with Stratoshift's delivery lead about a problem he mentioned, then reviews his latest checkpoint report and updates the stage plan with actuals and a revised forecast. Which 'controlling a stage' activity is she carrying out?
A.why: Evaluate work package status combines informal conversations with the team manager, a review of the checkpoint report and an update of the stage plan with actuals and forecasts (16.4.2).

whyNot.0: Evaluate stage status compares the whole stage's progress with the stage plan; the actions described focus on one team's work package.
whyNot.2: Receive completed work package deals with a work package handed back as finished; this one is still being executed.
whyNot.3: Capture issues and risks registers and assesses a new issue or risk; Mairi is reviewing progress on the work package.

A.q: On Project Skyline, Mairi Campbell finds that a two-week slip in the pilot wave can be recovered inside stage tolerance by re-ordering later work. She selects that solution in the 'take corrective action' activity. Which role should be accountable for this activity?
A.why: In the RACI for take corrective action, the executive is accountable while the project manager is responsible for doing the work (16.6, table 16.2).

whyNot.0: Mairi is responsible: she collects the facts and selects the solution, but accountability sits with the executive.
whyNot.1: Project assurance is not involved in the take corrective action activity.
whyNot.3: Project support is informed of corrective action, not accountable for it.

A.q: Stratoshift returns a completed work package of runbooks for the pilot wave. The product descriptions name the head of IT operations as the approver for each runbook. Before updating the product register, Mairi Campbell checks that he has signed them off. Which 'controlling a stage' activity is this?
A.why: In receive completed work package the PM makes sure each product has the approval set out in its product description, then updates the product register and stage plan (16.4.3).

whyNot.1: Evaluate work package status reviews progress while the work is under way; here the work package has been returned complete.
whyNot.2: Authorize a work package starts work by agreeing a work package with the team manager; this work is finished.
whyNot.3: Evaluate stage status compares the stage as a whole with its plan; checking product approvals belongs to receiving the work package.

B.q: On Project Skyline, Mairi Campbell decides to amend Stratoshift's work package to recover a delay that sits within stage tolerance. The project board wants to know who must be told once the corrective action is taken. Under the RACI for 'take corrective action', which role should be informed?
B.why: Project support is informed in the take corrective action activity, so that registers and records reflect the action (16.6, table 16.2).

whyNot.0: Project assurance is not involved in take corrective action.
whyNot.1: The business layer is not involved in take corrective action; it deals with project-level tolerances.
whyNot.2: The executive is accountable for take corrective action, which is more than being informed.

B.q: Mairi Campbell now forecasts that the wave migration stage will finish five weeks late, beyond the four weeks of time tolerance the board set for the stage. What should she produce, and in which activity?
options: An exception plan, in 'escalate issues and risks'
An exception report, in 'escalate issues and risks'
An issue report, in 'take corrective action'
B.why: A forecast breach of stage tolerance is escalated to the board with an exception report in escalate issues and risks (16.4.7, 11.3.1).

whyNot.0: An exception plan is prepared in managing a stage boundary, and only after the board asks for one in response to the exception report.
whyNot.2: Corrective action is for deviations the PM can resolve inside stage tolerance; this one breaks it.
whyNot.3: A highlight report is the routine time-driven report; a forecast breach needs the event-driven exception report.

B.q: On Project Skyline, project support gathers the figures and drafts most of each highlight report, and Mairi Campbell checks it and sends it to the board. Under the RACI for 'report highlights', which role is responsible?
B.why: The project manager is responsible for report highlights, even when support helps to compile it (16.4.8, 16.6 table 16.2).

whyNot.0: Project support is consulted in report highlights; helping to draft does not make it responsible.
whyNot.1: The team manager is consulted, mainly through the checkpoint reports that feed the highlight report.
whyNot.3: Project assurance is consulted in report highlights, not responsible for producing them.

C.q: Arjun Menon warns that his work package will exceed its time tolerance by a week. Mairi Campbell can absorb the delay within stage tolerance by re-ordering later work, but she raises an exception report to the board asking for direction. Is this an appropriate application of the 'escalate issues and risks' activity, and why?
options: Yes, because the team manager has forecast a breach of work package tolerance
Yes, because a forecast exception should be reported as soon as it is known
No, because the deviation can be resolved inside the stage tolerance
No, because the team manager should raise the exception report himself
C.why: Only exceptions to the stage or project plan go to the board. A work package breach that the PM can absorb inside stage tolerance is handled by corrective action in controlling a stage (11.2.6, 16.4.6, 16.4.7).

whyNot.0: A forecast breach of work package tolerance is raised by the team manager to the PM as an issue; it does not by itself justify an exception report to the board.
whyNot.1: Exceptions are reported on a forecast, but here no stage tolerance is forecast to be exceeded, so there is no exception for the board.
whyNot.3: Team managers escalate to the PM; exception reports go from the PM to the board.

C.q: For the foundations stage, Mairi Campbell writes the work package description for Stratoshift's landing zone work on her own and emails it to Arjun Menon with a start date, without discussing it with him. Is this an appropriate application of the 'authorize a work package' activity, and why?
options: Yes, because the project manager authorizes work packages in this activity
Yes, because the description sets the scope, cost and time tolerances
No, because the description should be co-created with the team manager
No, because the executive should approve each work package description
C.why: The recommended actions for authorize a work package include co-creating and reviewing the work package with the team manager and confirming acceptance before authorizing the start (16.4.1).

whyNot.0: The PM does authorize work packages here, but that does not explain why issuing one without the team manager is acceptable; it is not.
whyNot.1: Work package tolerances are scope, cost and time, but setting them does not remove the need to agree the package with the team manager.
whyNot.3: Work packages are authorized by the PM, not the executive; the failing is the lack of co-creation.

C.q: Each month Mairi Campbell assembles information from Stratoshift's checkpoint reports, the project log and any changes to the stage plan, lists the corrective actions taken, and sends the board a highlight report at the frequency set in the communication management approach. Is this an appropriate application of the 'report highlights' activity, and why?
options: Yes, because it follows the recommended actions at the agreed frequency
Yes, because highlight reports are event-driven controls for the board
No, because corrective actions should be reported in an exception report
No, because the checkpoint reports should go directly to the board
C.why: Report highlights assembles checkpoint reports, the project log and stage plan revisions, lists corrective actions and issues the highlight report at the frequency in the communication management approach (16.4.8).

whyNot.1: The verdict is right but the reason is wrong: highlight reports are time-driven controls, not event-driven.
whyNot.2: Corrective actions inside tolerance are listed in the highlight report; an exception report is for a forecast tolerance breach.
whyNot.3: Checkpoint reports go from the team manager to the PM; the board receives the highlight report.

reteach.title: Three jobs, eight activities
reteach.question: If you think of controlling a stage as three jobs (run the work packages, watch and report, deal with problems), where does each activity sit?

blocks.body: Run the work packages: authorize a work package, evaluate work package status, receive completed work package. Watch and report: evaluate stage status, report highlights. Deal with problems: capture issues and risks, take corrective action, escalate issues and risks. In a question, ask which job the PM is doing, then which step of that job.

blocks.caption: Evaluating stage status can reveal the need for new or amended work, which loops back to authorize a work package.

blocks.text: Remember the two RACI anchors: report highlights (PM responsible; team manager, support and assurance consulted) and take corrective action (executive accountable; project support informed).

explain.body: Authorize a work package is triggered by a new stage or by corrective action, and covers new packages or amendments to existing ones. The PM co-creates it with the team manager. Evaluate work package status keeps in touch while the work runs. Receive completed work package checks approvals and updates the product register.

test.q: On Project Skyline, Mairi Campbell has chosen to recover a delay inside stage tolerance. She now meets Arjun Menon to agree higher cost and time tolerances for his existing work package and confirm he accepts the change. Which activity is she using?
test.why: Corrective action is put into effect through authorize a work package, which covers amendments to existing work packages as well as new ones (16.4.1, 16.4.6).

whyNot.0: The corrective action has already been chosen; agreeing the amended package with the team manager is done in authorize a work package.
whyNot.1: Evaluate work package status reviews progress; it does not change the agreed tolerances.
whyNot.2: The issue was captured earlier; this step is agreeing the amended work package.

explain.body: Capture issues and risks registers each new issue or risk and then assesses it before any decision. If the PM can fix it inside stage tolerance, take corrective action selects a solution. If stage tolerance is forecast to be exceeded, escalate issues and risks sends an exception report to the board.

test.q: Stratoshift reports that a security tool licence may not arrive in time for the landing zone build. Mairi Campbell immediately asks the board to fund a different tool before recording or assessing the risk. Which recommended action of 'capture issues and risks' has she skipped?
options: Send an exception report to the board
Register the risk and assess its impact
Agree a new work package with the team
test.why: Before deciding on a course of action, each issue or risk should be registered and then assessed for its impact (16.4.5).

whyNot.0: An exception report is for a forecast breach of stage tolerance, which has not been established; the missing step is registering and assessing.
whyNot.2: Agreeing a new work package is how corrective action is applied, after the risk has been captured and assessed.
whyNot.3: Highlight frequency is set in the communication management approach and is unrelated to capturing a new risk.

explain.body: Evaluate stage status compares actual progress with the stage plan and can trigger corrective action. Report highlights gives the board a summary of stage and project status, assembled from checkpoint reports, the project log and stage plan changes, at the frequency set in the communication management approach.

test.q: Brennan Mutual's audit committee asks Mairi Campbell how she decided to send highlight reports to the project board every month. Where is the frequency of highlight reporting documented?
options: In each team manager's checkpoint report
In the work package descriptions for the stage
In the risk management approach in the PID
test.why: The PM issues highlight reports at the frequency documented in the communication management approach, as part of the project controls (16.4.8).

whyNot.1: Checkpoint reports are inputs to the highlight report; they do not set how often the board is reported to.
whyNot.2: Work package descriptions set the checkpoint frequency for each team, not the highlight frequency for the board.
whyNot.3: The risk management approach sets risk procedures, scales and responsibilities, not reporting frequency to the board.

explain.body: Report highlights: the PM is responsible; the team manager, project support and project assurance are consulted. Take corrective action: the executive is accountable, the PM responsible and project support informed; the business layer and project assurance are not involved.

test.q: Brennan Mutual's chief risk officer wants project assurance to sign off every corrective action Mairi Campbell takes inside stage tolerance. Which statement about the RACI for 'take corrective action' is correct?
options: Project assurance is consulted and the PM is accountable
The executive is accountable and assurance is not involved
The business layer is informed and the PM is accountable
Project support is responsible and the executive is consulted
test.why: For take corrective action the executive is accountable, the PM responsible and project support informed; project assurance and the business layer are not involved (16.6, table 16.2).

whyNot.0: Project assurance is not involved in take corrective action, and the PM is responsible rather than accountable.
whyNot.2: The business layer is not involved, and accountability sits with the executive.
whyNot.3: Project support is informed, not responsible; the PM does the work.
